subject: Does renjin support Big Data and how scalable it is

messages.author: 88402a6f402011b6
messages.subject: Does renjin support Big Data and how scalable it is
parts:
Hi Team,

 

We are trying to develop predictive Analytic tool but we want to do it on java based platform.

 

Then heard about Renjin. I found it very interesting.

 

But there is not much tutorial regarding this on google.

 

So I want to clarify few things  like

 

1.)    As Its runs on JVM then it will not have memory problem that R has? Please confirm

2.)    How much data it can process. Will it fit with big data implementation?

3.)    What sort of API it offers?

4.) How scalable it is ?

 

Thanks,

Chandra

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Does renjin support Big Data and how scalable it is
parts:
Hi Chandra,
"Big data" and "scalable" mean different things to different people :-)

I'd suggest taking a look at http://docs.renjin.org for an introduction to development with Renjin. With regard to how Renjin aims to address R's "memory problem", you might find the blog post on Renjin's Vector Pipeliner of interest:
http://www.renjin.org/blog/2013-07-30-deep-dive-vector-pipeliner.html

I'd also suggest doing your own benchmarking to verify that Renjin will meet your needs. If for any reason you find Renjin deficient in running your particular benchmarks, I'd encourage you to submit them to the renjin-benchmarks project so we can continue to improve Renjin's handling of large analysis problems.

Good luck!

Alex
